newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy plans budget confidence vote - statement.
newsitem.headline: Italy plans budget confidence vote - statement.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government plans to call a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament on its 1997 mini-budget, Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said on Monday.

A statement issued after a cabinet meeting did not say when the motion would be called, but a parliamentary timetable released last week indicated a confidence vote was expected for Tuesday. Prodi relies on the hard-left Communist Refoundation for his lower house majority.

The budget is designed to cut 15.5 trillion lire ($9.1 billion) from this year's budget deficit in a bid to meet tough criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for founder members of the planned European single currency.

The package has been bitterly criticised by the centre-right Freedom Alliance opposition, and even by centrists within Prodi's own coalition, for demanding early payment of taxes by companies on their severance payment funds.

Some amendments have been introduced, but others are still pending. A confidence vote will sweep these away and allow the bill to move to the Senate (upper house) for approval. Under Italian law, the budget must be approved by both houses of parliament before the end of May.

Prodi has called around 20 confidence votes since taking office a year ago to side-step opposition filibustering on a wide range of legislation. If his administration loses a vote it would automatically be forced to resign.
